subject: Post-call: model-fit next steps & parity acceptance thresholds
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie@finset.com>, Jorge Alvarez <jorge@finset.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: model-fit next steps & parity acceptance thresholds

Thanks again for taking the time today — quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum. High-level notes from our discovery: FinSet needs a conversational assistant for underwriting workflows (short Q&A + multi-step form filling) and a document summarization path for investor decks. Primary concerns: hallucination risk on financial language, latency constraints for an in-app experience, and data residency for PII-containing test sets.

Recap & immediate recommendations:
- Models to trial (recommended):
  1) Open candidate: Open-Llama-3-16B (q4f quantized) — low cost, good instruction-following baseline.
  2) Redwood baseline: Redwood-Prod-7B (production-tuned) — lower hallucination profile historically on financial prompts; serves as the parity baseline.
- Acceptance thresholds (proposed):
  - Intent/extraction accuracy >= 95% on the short-form QA set
  - Factual hallucination rate < 1% (defined by gold fact checks in prompt set)
  - Summarization ROUGE-L >= 0.62 on the deck-summary set
  - Latency: p95 generation latency < 350ms for 512-token limit on Dedicated capacity (can relax on hosted)
- Evaluation artifacts I attached: prompt bundle (finset_prompt_bundle_v1.jsonl) and anchor benchmark CSV (finset_bench_results_anchor.csv) with initial pass/fail examples and expected labels.

Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood runs an initial benchmark (we use your sample data + our prompt bundle) — 48–72 hour turnaround for bench run.
2) Two-week trial plan: A/B between Open-Llama-3-16B (quantized) and Redwood-Prod-7B using 1k annotated prompts across short, multi-turn, and document summary buckets.
3) Acceptance review: joint readout with FinSet on metrics + failure modes (we'll provide a severity classification and example failures).

Can you confirm (a) you're OK with the proposed acceptance thresholds and (b) share the 1k sample set or a redacted export we should use for the bench? Once confirmed I'll kick off the evaluation and loop in Priyom to configure the harness.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

From: Sophie Lang <sophie@finset.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jorge Alvarez <jorge@finset.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: model-fit next steps & parity acceptance thresholds

Thanks Neha — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we share the sample set:
- Latency: the in-app flow needs p95 <= 300ms for 256-token responses. You mentioned 350ms for 512; can you provide expected numbers for 256 token targets on both models (dedicated vs hosted)?
- Data residency: can the bench run be performed inside our VPC/demo environment? We cannot send PII outside our infra for the initial trial.
- Regression monitoring: you've called out a hallucination threshold — how will Redwood detect regressions daily during the trial? Alerting cadence?

Also, what's the expected cost for the two-week dedicated trial (estimate) so we can review with procurement.

— Sophie
Sophie Lang | Head of ML, FinSet
sophie@finset.com

---

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Lang <sophie@finset.com>, Jorge Alvarez <jorge@finset.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call: model-fit next steps & parity acceptance thresholds

Internal/tech notes (for Neha/Marissa and to answer Sophie's latency/regression questions):
- Latency estimates (lab + Dedicated):
  - Open-Llama-3-16B (q4f) on Dedicated (A100 equiv): p50 ~ 45ms, p95 ~ 220ms for 256-token generation; for 512 tokens expect p95 ~ 350ms.
  - Redwood-Prod-7B (int8 optimized): p50 ~ 35ms, p95 ~ 180ms for 256 tokens; p95 ~ 300–320ms for 512 tokens.
- Data residency: we can run the bench inside FinSet's VPC via Redwood Private package (we'll provision a temporary evaluation environment; no external egress unless you enable it).
- Regression monitoring approach:
  1) Automated daily evals on the annotated 1k holdout set — compute per-metric deltas and sample failing examples.
  2) Severity-based alerting: critical (hallucination >1.5% absolute change) triggers paging to on-call; important (accuracy delta >3%) triggers Slack summary + ticket.
  3) We keep an audit log (per-request hashes + model version) for postmortem if needed.
- Canary/rollout plan: start canary at 5% traffic for 48 hours; if metrics stable, ramp to 25% then 100%. Fallback to Redwood-Prod-7B automatically on error-rate or p95 breaches.

I'll draft a short eval harness config and a suggested prompt-sampling split (40% short QA / 40% multi-turn / 20% document summary).

— Priyom
Priyom Das | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie@finset.com>, Jorge Alvarez <jorge@finset.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: model-fit next steps & parity acceptance thresholds

Great questions — answers inline and next steps below.

- Latency for 256 tokens: based on Priyom's lab runs, both models hit your target on Dedicated (p95: Open-Llama-3-16B ~220ms; Redwood-Prod-7B ~180ms). If you prefer a conservative SLA we can target p95 <= 300ms for the trial.
- Data residency: we will provision a temporary Redwood Private evaluation node in your VPC. The bench will run inside FinSet infra and results/metrics are pushed to your internal metrics endpoint (no PII leaves unless you opt in).
- Regression monitoring: daily automated runs against the holdout and an alerting policy as Priyom described. We'll provide a Slack channel + weekly readout cadence; immediate paging only for critical breaches.

Cost estimate for two-week Dedicated trial (approx):
- Dedicated evaluation node (1x A100-equivalent, 2 weeks): $8,500
- Engineering support (setup + baseline bench run): $2,500
- Total est: $11,000 (one-time trial invoice) — we can convert to a committed credit if you proceed to a reserved Dedicated contract.

Planned next steps if this looks good to you:
1) FinSet shares redacted 1k sample set or grant us access to the test bucket (we can accept a GCS/S3 presigned link or run inside VPC).
2) We provision the Private eval node and run the anchor benchmark (48–72 hours).
3) Joint readout and decision on canary/rollout.

Attachments: finset_prompt_bundle_v1.jsonl (prompt sets + labeling spec), finset_bench_results_anchor.csv (anchor examples and expected labels).

If you confirm sample access and budget, I'll send a one-page engagement order and we can kick off the trial this week. Proposed times for kick-off call (30 min): Tue 09/21 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed 09/22 14:00–14:30 PT.

Thanks,
Neha
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

From: Sophie Lang <sophie@finset.com>

Cc: Jorge Alvarez <jorge@finset.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: model-fit next steps & parity acceptance thresholds

Sounds good — we can provide a redacted 1k export (no raw PII). Procurement has penciled in the trial budget but needs the one-page engagement order and the DocuSign. Please send the order and we'll aim to start the kick-off on Tue 09/21 10:00 PT.

Also — two asks for the bench: please include a per-example failure reason tag in outputs (e.g., hallucination|partial_answer|format_error) and include a short list of top-10 failing prompts after the first run so our team can triage quickly.

Appreciate it — Sophie
Sophie Lang | Head of ML, FinSet
sophie@finset.com
